candidate_datasets_from_prompt.classification: Reference dataset only (per-unit cost column of interest) -- NOT currently ingestible in a correct/meaningful way
candidate_datasets_from_prompt.evidence: 185,013 rows, columns: Customer ID, Customer Status, Date Order was placed, Delivery Date, Order ID, Product ID, Quantity Ordered, Total Retail Price for This Order, Cost Price Per Unit. 0 duplicate Order IDs, 0 negative Cost Price Per Unit, no currency column, dates in 'DD-Mon-YY' format. Traced the actual field resolution if this file were fed through GENERIC_COLUMN_MAP: order_date resolves via the fuzzy 'date' fallback to 'Date Order was placed' (correct); quantity resolves via the fuzzy 'qty' fallback to 'Quantity Ordered' (correct); BUT gross_revenue AND unit_price BOTH resolve via the shared 'amount' fallback role to the SAME first-matching column, 'Total Retail Price for This Order' (an order-level total, not a real unit price) -- meaning if ingested, unit_price would be silently set equal to the whole order's total price, not a per-unit figure. 'Cost Price Per Unit' -- the one column that would genuinely solve the COGS-availability gap -- has NO fallback role at all (unit_cogs is only resolved via a literal map match, and none of the 3 existing maps have a literal header matching this file's column names), so it would never be picked up even if this file were ingested. sku/external_order_id/channel/customer_email also have no literal match for this file's headers and no fallback role, so no OrderItem row would ever be written and no COGS would ever be captured.
candidate_datasets_from_prompt.verdict: Do NOT use for ingestion testing in Prompt 2 as-is -- confirmed via code-level field-resolution tracing (not assumption) that attempting to ingest this file today would silently produce an incorrect unit_price (= order total) and would NOT actually pick up the real per-unit cost data despite that column's presence. This corrects Scanwick_QA_Testing_Scripts.md's characterization of 'Cost Price Per Unit' as merely 'currently unused' -- it is currently unusable without a code change (no unit_cogs fallback role, no matching literal map), not simply unreferenced.

This is a build-completeness gap that will directly affect how Prompt 2 (Ingestion Testing) must be executed (via direct function calls, matching this project's own test suite's pattern, not via a real HTTP upload flow).
The Olist adapter (ecommerce_olist_adapter.py) exists and is correctly implemented against GENERIC_COLUMN_MAP, but is never wired to any route or ingestion trigger -- confirmed via whole-repo grep.

Scanwick_QA_Testing_Scripts.md's characterization of the Olist set ('has no generic_csv/Shopify/WooCommerce column map of its own yet') is stale relative to the current repository state -- the adapter now exists; only the wiring is missing.
ingestion_blockers: None of the 3 datasets recommended for Prompt 2 are blocked from ingestion at the data-quality level (all 3 are clean or degrade gracefully). The blocker is purely architectural: no HTTP/Celery trigger path exists for any Ecommerce source, so Prompt 2 must invoke the ingestion functions directly in Python, exactly as this repository's own test suite already does.
implementation_gaps: No products/customers table exists anywhere in the schema -- sku is a free-text string with no catalog/normalization, and customer identity is a deterministic email-hash UUID, not a real customer entity.

unit_cogs has no fuzzy-fallback role at all -- only a literal header match across 3 fixed maps can ever populate it; any dataset with a real cost-per-unit column under a different header name (e.g. archive (19)/orders.csv's 'Cost Price Per Unit') will never have it picked up without a code change.

The Olist adapter discards Olist's real order_status column entirely -- flatten_olist_dataset's output has no status-bearing column, so every Olist order that would be ingested through this adapter falls through _resolve_generic_status's refund_amount check (which is also never populated, since refund_amount isn't in the flattened output either) and is unconditionally assigned OrderStatus.fulfilled, regardless of its real status. Quantified: 2,963 of 99,441 real Olist orders (2.98%) have a non-'delivered' real status (625 canceled, 609 unavailable, 314 invoiced, 301 processing, 1,107 shipped, 5 created, 2 approved) -- all of which would be mislabeled 'fulfilled' if this adapter were ever actually invoked. This is a genuine data-fidelity gap in the adapter's design, not a bug in the shared ingestion path (the adapter simply never attempted to carry this field over).
